newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan January industrial output.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan January industrial output.

text.p: The following is a selection of economists' reactions to Japan's industrial production for January, which showed a preliminary 5.3 percent rise from December on a seasonally adjusted basis.
The figure was a bit higher compared with a Reuters poll of economists which had shown an average forecast of a 4.9 percent rise.
MIKIHIRO MATSUOKA, SENIOR ECONOMIST, DAIWA INSTITUTE OF RESEARCH:
"The January increase is in accordance with the market consensus. But the (forecast fall) for February and March will cancel out any increase in January."
The Trade Ministry forecast that February output would fall 3.3 percent month-on-month and March by 2.7 percent.
PETER MORGAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, HSBC JAMES CAPEL JAPAN, TOKYO:

"We are seeing a lot of the pre-tax consumption demand coming through. In particular we've already had indications that automobile output was quite strong in January and this has been done in advance of anticipated sales in February and March, so that I would expect that production would be scaled back in the next couple of months from this quite large increase."
The Japanese government plans to raise the consumption tax from three percent to five percent from April 1.
KYOHEI MORITA, ECONOMIST, NOMURA RESEARCH INSTITUTE:

"The January figure is largely in line with expectations, but the forecasts for February and March are rather weak. Although the (forecast) decline is partly due to the strong January number, it also reflects the uncertainty held by firms over the economic outlook beyond April.
"Businesses cannot maintain a clear outlook on the economy as they want to see the effects of fiscal tightening measures to be taken from April."
